races.title: State Senate, District 4
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Alexandra Duarte
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Senate District 4. Farmer who, with her husband John, grew almonds and walnuts on the family farm in Modesto, where they raised their children. She has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists voter guide recommendations from Based in Malibu (Sway voting group) and Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Alexandra Duarte was born or raised, or when she came to California. We found no record of elected office, legislative work or a policy or budget career. We found no documented stance on data centers or development, and no actions in office, since she has not held office. Her site and Ballotpedia say nothing on immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, school choice, or limits on investor or foreign land buyers. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and the endorsements listed there are only voter-guide recommendations. We found no news reporting on her.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Her campaign site describes her as a farmer who grew almonds and walnuts on the family farm in Modesto. It lists no elected office, and Ballotpedia lists none.
qual.why: Farming is real-world work, but the sources give no business size, management role, policy job or legislative record to rate against this office, so no score is given.
qual.label: Background not found: unknown, not unqualified

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says she believes shoplifting is a crime and criminals belong in jail. She says she supports investing more in law enforcement and stricter sentencing for dangerous criminals.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Her campaign site says she supports cutting taxes and cutting fraud and abuse from the state budget. It does not mention property or homestead taxes specifically.

cands.name: Jaron Brandon
cands.bio: Two-term Tuolumne County Supervisor and former Chair of the Board of Supervisors. Raised in Tuolumne County and first in his family to graduate college (UC Merced, political science, 2015). Worked several years in technology before returning home. Democratic candidate for State Senate District 4 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions AFL-CIO, California Teachers Association, IUOE Local 3, Equality California, California Young Democrats and California Mountain Biking Coalition, per Ballotpedia's endorsement list.

His survey and campaign site name State Treasurer Fiona Ma, Senate Majority Leader Lena Gonzalez, former Insurance Commissioner Dave Jones, and several local officials including the Mayor of Merced and county supervisors from El Dorado, Stanislaus and Calaveras counties.

cands.gaps: We found no stated positions or actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, gun laws, abortion, immigration enforcement or H-1B, or school choice. The campaign policy page showed none of its 21 policy sections, and the About page was cut off partway through its infrastructure section. We found no independent news reporting or county records to check the county accomplishments he and his campaign describe, such as the pay raises, housing approvals and budget reforms. His exact birth date and the specific town of his birth were not found. No controversies were found in the pages reviewed.

local.label: Roots 100: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey he says he was born and raised in a rural trailer park in Tuolumne County, and Ballotpedia lists Sonora Union High School as his high school.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Second-term Tuolumne County Supervisor and past Board Chair, with several years of earlier work in technology and retail; BA in Political Science from UC Merced (2015). The campaign says he has served about five years on the board.
qual.why: Local elected office that included county budget decisions fits the middle band. He has no state legislative service and no law or policy career on the record reviewed.
qual.label: Local elected office that included county budget decisions fits the middle band. He has no state legislative service and no law or policy career on the record reviewed.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he approved two large bargaining contracts that raised Sheriff's deputy pay by about 24%, restored Captain ranks, funded a $1.8 million dispatch center, and backed re-establishing the Tuolumne Narcotics Team. This is the campaign's own account and was not checked against county records.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign site says he approved every housing project that came before him and cut red tape on ADUs, conditional zonings and lot sizes. His survey says he wants to build all kinds of housing at scale and speed up projects. These are self-reported claims.
